newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian shares fall further, rate of slide eases.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian shares fall further, rate of slide eases.

text.p: Nigerian blue chip shares furthered their recent slide on Thursday, but the pace was more gentle than earlier in the week, traders said.
The Nigerian stock market's all-share index fell to 8148.40 from 8157.89 on Wednesday.
"The shares are falling basically because there is no money in the economy," one trader said.
Dealers said trading for leading shares was steady, and big recent fallers in the oil, food and conglomerates sectors closed unchanged.
But Nestle at 50.70 naira, BOC Gases at 15.30 naira were each down 20 kobo.
Total fell five kobo to 54.85 naira.
Conglomerates UAC slid nine kobo to 14.06 naira and Lever Brothers dipped five kobo to 24.40 naira.
West African Portland Cement Company (WAPCO) dropped 10 kobo to 60.10 naira. Nigerian Bottling Company was down 10 kobo at 49.90 naira.
Tyre maker Dunlop was seven kobo lower at 9.60 naira due to lack of interest, dealers said.
The only big drop in the banking sector was by Guaranty Trust Bank, down five kobo at 5.50 naira.
Afribank was up one kobo to 3.84 naira, a similar gain to Owena Bank which finished at 1.45 naira. Co-operative Bank was two kobo higher at 1.15 naira
Healthcare firm Smithkline Beecham strengthened by 15 kobo to 5.65 naira.
Insurer AIICO edged higher to 15.20 naira, adding 15 kobo after its well-received first quarter result.
United Nigerian Textile also closed 10 kobo up at 5.80 on rising demand.
